how can i apple online for learning licence
ChatGPT said:

Here’s how you can apply online for a Learner’s Licence (LL) in India:

1️⃣ Go to the Official Portal

The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways has a central website:
https://parivahan.gov.in/parivahan/

  1. On the homepage, hover over “Online Services”.

  2. Click “Driving Licence Related Services”.

2️⃣ Select Your State

You’ll be redirected to Sarathi Parivahan. Select the state where you want to apply (this is important because rules and fees can vary slightly by state).

3️⃣ Apply for Learner’s Licence

  1. Click “Apply for Learner Licence” under the menu.

  2. Read the instructions carefully and click “Continue”.

  3. Fill out the application form:

    • Personal details (name, address, DOB)

    • RTO office selection

    • Type of vehicle (MCWG, LMV, etc.)

  4. Upload required documents:

    • Age proof (Aadhaar, PAN, Birth Certificate)

    • Address proof (Aadhaar, Passport, Voter ID)

    • Passport size photograph

    • Signature (scanned)

  5. Pay the applicable fee online (usually ₹150–₹200 depending on state).

4️⃣ Book Your Test Slot

After payment, the system will allow you to book an online test slot at your RTO. Many states now also offer an online LL test from home (webcam + mic required).

5️⃣ Take the Test

  • It’s a basic test of road signs, rules, and regulations.

  • Pass marks are usually 60%.

  • If you pass, you get an e-Learner’s Licence immediately for download or it will be posted to your address.

6️⃣ Download Your Learner’s Licence

You can download a soft copy from the same portal under “Print Learner’s Licence”.

Quick Tips

  • Use your Aadhaar number for easy verification.

  • Keep your documents scanned in JPEG or PDF format under 200 KB.

  • Prepare for the test: Mock Test Link (official).

You said:
what is lmv
ChatGPT said:

“LMV” stands for Light Motor Vehicle.

In the context of a driving or learner’s licence in India:

  • LMV (NT) → Light Motor Vehicle (Non-Transport)

    • For private vehicles such as cars, jeeps, small vans, SUVs, etc. used for personal (non-commercial) purposes.

  • LMV (TR) → Light Motor Vehicle (Transport)

    • For light commercial vehicles like taxis, delivery vans, small goods carriers — used for commercial purposes.

So, if you’re applying for a learner’s licence to drive a private car, you should select LMV (NT).

ChatGPT said:

This is the “Application-cum-Declaration as to Physical Fitness” section you’ll see when filling a learner’s licence or driving licence form in India (Form 1).
It’s basically a self-declaration about your health to confirm you’re fit to drive safely.

Here’s what each point means:

QuestionWhat it’s askingWhy
(a) Epilepsy / sudden loss of consciousness / giddinessDo you have any condition that can cause you to faint or lose control suddenly?Such conditions make driving unsafe.
(b) Able to distinguish with each eyeCan you see properly with both eyes?Basic vision test for safe driving.
(b.i) Exception if you’ve lost one eye after 5 years driving experienceSpecial case: if you already had a licence for 5+ years and later lost one eye, you can still drive a light motor vehicle (private) if you have an outside mirror on the steering side.Allows experienced drivers with one eye to continue driving private cars.
(c) Lost hand/foot or muscular control defectDo you have any limb loss or muscular disability that affects your ability to control a vehicle?Physical ability to operate vehicle safely.
(d) Night blindnessCan you see at night?Important for driving in low light conditions.
(e) DeafnessAre you so deaf that you cannot hear ordinary sound signals (horns)? If applying for LMV, do you manage with or without a hearing aid?Being able to hear horns and sirens is important.
(f) Other diseases or disabilitiesAny other condition making you a danger to the public while driving? If yes, specify.Catch-all question.

How you should fill it:

  • Tick “NO” for all questions if you are medically fit.

  • Tick “YES” only if you actually have the condition mentioned.

  • If you tick “YES” for any, you’ll likely have to provide a Medical Certificate (Form 1A) signed by a registered medical practitioner.

  • For most healthy applicants, everything is “NO”.

ChatGPT said:

Got it — that message you’re seeing is from the Sarathi Parivahan portal.
It appears only if, in the physical fitness declaration, at least one of the answers is marked “YES” (even by mistake).

Here’s why and how to fix it:

1️⃣ Why it happened

  • In the online form, if you select “YES” for epilepsy, night blindness, deafness, loss of limbs, etc., the system automatically flags you as “physically unfit” because you declared a medical condition that makes you unsafe to drive.

  • Even if you clicked “YES” accidentally, it gets treated as a disqualification for a learner’s licence unless you apply under a special “physically challenged” category and upload a medical certificate.

2️⃣ How to correct it

  • Check your answers: Re-open the application (or start a fresh one) and ensure all answers are “NO” if you are healthy and medically fit to drive.

  • Save and submit again: This time the application will go through.

3️⃣ If you really have a condition (physically challenged)

  • In the same section there’s an option to select your “Physically Challenged” category or a suitable ADPVEH COV (Adapted Vehicle Class of Vehicle) — for example, if you use a specially adapted vehicle.

  • You’ll then need to upload a medical certificate (Form 1A) from a registered medical practitioner and possibly an RTO medical board clearance.

  • Only after that can your application be processed.

4️⃣ Quick steps

  1. Log back into Sarathi → “Application Status” → click “Edit Application”.

  2. Go to “Self Declaration on Physical Fitness” section.

  3. Select “NO” for all conditions if you are normal/fit.

  4. Save and resubmit.

If the portal won’t let you edit, you can cancel and create a new application (there’s no penalty if you haven’t paid yet).

CSS

Add this to your stylesheet:

css
.medal img {
  width: 20px;       /* size of the medal */
  height: 20px;
  vertical-align: middle; /* aligns with text baseline */
  margin-left: 5px;  /* small gap from the text */
}

This will make the medal icon:

  • Small like an emoji.

  • Vertically centered with your text.

  • With a tiny space between text and icon.
